significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) law-like decomposition: multilingual factual inconsistency consists of two additive components, and "the size of the residual (not the total) is what scales with script/typological distance," coupled to a form-(ii) mechanism in which baseline and residual errors arise at separable mid- and late-layer loci. This would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a causal decomposition, fixing expectations about which inconsistency should vary with language distance and which intervention locus should repair each error class; that bears directly on the interpretation of measurements built around resources such as mLAMA (Kassner et al., 2021) and factual-consistency analyses such as Fierro and Søgaard (2022). The negative branches are also informative: a small baseline would support treating most disagreement as language-specific, while shared loci or equal distance dependence would rule out the proposed two-component explanation; verified-true and verified-false therefore denote clearly distinct worlds. In the topic-substitution check, generic claims about language-independent versus language-specific mechanisms would merit about 5, whereas the quoted additive decomposition, differential scaling relation, and ordered causal loci are specific to this claim and justify the higher score.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "language-specific residual," defined as cross-lingual disagreement beyond the pooled within-language paraphrase baseline, which can serve as a measurable audit metric and can separate whether interventions reduce language-specific failure or ordinary prompt instability. It is post hoc with respect to individual QA failures, but the claim explicitly makes it an ex-ante release-gating handle through "model-release consistency claims, and factuality/safety audits should report the paraphrase-controlled residual," leaving an action window before deployment. After per-model re-estimation, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—only the residual should scale with script/typological distance—and a design constraint about separately targeting mid-layer baseline errors and late-layer residual errors, rather than merely supplying a procedure to rediscover an unconstrained direction; its asserted scope is multilingual factual QA across language and model families, not arbitrary tasks or modalities. The topic-substitution check lowers the generic multilingual-representation topic to the median, while the residual metric, distance relation, and release-audit use are claim-specific and give auditors and model developers downstream uptake beyond the immediate interpretability study.
